t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in three panels. Left: a deep navy column with a small wordmark, eyebrow and a large light-weight sans headline with a short lead. Centre: warm limestone field with a faint construction grid and a large navy hairline line drawing of a polypropylene pipe crossing diagonally, its butt-fusion bead finely hatched, wall edges in steel blue, annotated with mono tags and dimension callouts. Right: five stacked steps divided by hairline rules, each with a huge light numeral and small mono code, for <CONTENT>. Square corners, no shadows.
signature_idea: One fusion joint drawn huge and dimensioned sits between the title and the steps, making the joint the hero of a pipe-to-turnover process.
strengths: shows the actual PP butt-fusion joint as a precise drawing
navy/limestone panels with one steel-blue accent are on-palette
numerals plus mono codes make steps scannable
weaknesses: rounded pill tags break the square-corner rule
invented standard ISO 13485 and dimensions shown on the drawing
dense hatching on the bead is heavier than the hairline system
tags J-01 duplicated and J-02 on the same joint
steps column is dense with small text
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone panels, light headline, huge light numerals, mono codes and one steel-blue accent fit; pill tags, heavy hatching and invented standards cost a point.
